lines.text: Ilse broke the seal herself. Her hands were shaking, and it wasn't the cold.
I've wanted to do this since I was eleven years old.
Beyond the door was a round room, older than the cathedral above it, older than anything I had seen in Aldcrown. The walls were bare stone. In the middle stood a Stone.
Not milk-white glass, like the Order's new one. Black. Cold. Exactly like the Stone I touched at sixteen, on the worst day of my life.
And it was cracked. Straight through its heart.
No. That's not... Aldric lit seven rings. It's the first thing every child in Aldmere learns. He lit seven, and they built a cathedral on the spot.
At the foot of the Stone, someone had carved words into the floor. Old words, in a script I couldn't read. Ilse could.
Here King Aldric set his hand upon the Stone, and it could not hold him, and it broke.
I, Auster, his Measurer, wrote seven. For men will kneel to a number. They will not kneel to a mystery.
Let no Stone ever break again. To that end, I have founded the Order of the Measure.
Nobody spoke for a long time. Ilse sat down on the floor in her torn dress and Oswin's cloak, as if her legs had been cut.
Three hundred years. Every child in the kingdom measured against a number that was never real. And the Order was founded by the man who wrote it down.
I put my hand on the black Stone. It was cold, and dead, and it felt like looking in a mirror.
A stone doesn't crack because it finds nothing. It cracks because it can't hold what it finds. Ilse told me that once, about me. Three hundred years ago, someone had thought it about him.
The first king of Aldmere hadn't lit seven rings. He had lit none. He built aqueducts. While he lived, the south never saw frost. He was like me.
So you're a king.
I'm a zero.
Apparently it's the same thing. That explains a great deal about kings.
I thought of the carving in the tunnels. A king, with no rings behind his head. Once, somebody had wanted to remember the truth.
My lord. If the Order was built to hide one hollow-born king, what has it been doing with all the others?
Nobody answered. Below us, the stream of light ran on down the stair. Down, to the place the Measurers called the farm.
The Lord Who Measured Zero. Chapter ninety-nine, coming soon.
